articleTitle: Development of Indonesia National Oceanographic Data Repository
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: This Indonesia National Oceanographic Data Center is a national data center designed as an oceanographic and marine data center for storing archives of oceanographic and marine data within Indonesia water. Currently, there are at least ten elements of oceanographic data included within our repository: Drifting Buoy, Undulating Ocean Recorded, Surface Only, Expendable Bathy-Thermograph, Conductivity Temperature Depth, Glider, Moored Buoy, Ocean Station, and Profiling Floats. This repository is accessible by communities and institutions as to tool for sharing data that supports query and visualization. The platform is built in compliance with international standards, and to be registered as part of IODE-UNESCO

articleTitle: Mangrove Extent and Change Mapping of Muaragembong from 1990 to 2020 using Google Earth Engine (GEE)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems have crucial functions in the sustainability of coastal areas. However, land conversion from mangrove forest to other land cover is unavoidable - including mangrove forest areas in Muaragembong, Kabupaten Bekasi, West Java, Indonesia. Muaragembong has been facing physical and anthropogenic threats to its sustainability. Mangrove forest monitoring is, therefore, fundamental to determine the preventive and responsive actions. This study analyzed the mangrove cover changes of Muaragembong for the last 30 years (1990–2020) using Google Earth Engine (GEE). The extraction of 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020 images was from Landsat 5 TM, Landsat 7 ETM+, Landsat 5 TM, and Landsat 8 OLI respectively. This study used Mangrove Vegetation Index (MVI) to enhance the images, which considers the greenness and humidity in its equation. The results showed that the mangrove areas in Muaragembong decreased from 1991 to 2000 (41.16%), gradually increased from 2000 to 2010 (20.05%), strongly increased from 2010 to 2020 (181.39%). The mangrove area of Muaragembong was 550.52 hectares in 1991, 323.91 hectares in 2000, 388.85 hectares in 2010, and 1,094 hectares in 2020. The trends followed the presence and absence of mangrove conservation actions in the given year or period.

articleTitle: Geoscience Application for Marine Pipe Line Identification and Validation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Indonesia as the largest archipelagic country in the world with a larger water area than the mainland has the potential of natural resources in the Ocean. This is a challenge for both exploration and exploitation. Underwater utilities are one of the solutions to connect the distribution of natural resources from sea to land. In the oil and gas industry, the distribution of oil and gas from the sea platform to the mainland is via undersea gas pipelines. Based on the regulation of the Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources no. 16 of 2020 CHAPTER III, the target for development and transmission of natural gas until 2024 is 17,300 km, including subsea pipelines. In addition, the Decree of the Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries No. 14 of 2021 strengthens the arrangement of submarine pipelines and cables in Indonesia. To arrange submarine cables and pipelines, it is necessary to update the condition of submarine pipelines and cables. The data can be used as a reference for action plans for the arrangement of existing pipelines and cables as well as the future construction of new lines. Geoscience methods such as Bathymetry, Side Scan Sonar, and Magnetic surveys can be applied to get an overview of the underwater pipeline conditions. The first stages are referring to secondary data from the Indonesian Navy Hydrographic and Oceanographic Center (PUSHIDROSAL) pipeline, and then determine the survey lines for bathymetry, side-scan sonar (SSS), and Magnetic. From the bathymetry data, the coordinates and estimates of objects in the form of pipes are obtained. The estimate object will be validated with the image from Side Scan Sonar. Furthermore, quantitative evidence of the object is carried out by observing the value of the magnetic anomaly. Bathymetry results in the research area (9301000 S- 9299500 Sand 224250 E - 227000 E) there is an object that is suspected to be piped. Then its overlapped with the SSS image, it is clear that the appearance of an object stretches along the path. Furthermore, it is validated with magnetic data at the location and shows a magnetic anomaly along with the suspected object. The graph of a high magnetic amplitude deviation indicates that the object contains metal (pipe).

articleTitle: Simple Analysis of Determination of Tidal Types of Sea Water: A Case Study in Lamong Bay Waters, East Java
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: The development of Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) on aspects of shoreline change, is always related to the character and dynamics of seawater in the coastal area. Changes in the forward (sedimentation) and retreat (erosion) of the coastline depending on the dynamics of seawater. These dynamics include ocean currents and ocean waves. In general, people often see tidal conditions of seawater. This paper aims to show the results of a tidal survey and a simple analysis to determine the type of tide. Tidal surveys have been carried out in Lamong Bay, East Java. The calculation and analysis of tidal parameters were have been conducted as well. The calculation results have been obtained in the form of a datum chart, namely HAT (Highest Astronomical Tide), MHHWS (Mean Highest High Water Spring), MHHWN (Mean Highest High Water Neap), MSL (Mean Sea Level), MLLWN (Mean lowest low Water Neap), MLLWS (Mean Lowest Low Water Spring), and LAT (Lowest Astronomical Tide). This simple analysis is intended to determine the type of tides just by looking at the footage of how many waves a day are there. If there is one wave a day then the tidal type is Diurnal, while if there are two waves in a day then the Semi-Diurnal type. The type of mixture will be displayed in the curve, if there are more than 1.5 waves a day then the type of mixture tends to be diurnal. On the other hand, if it is less than 1.5 waves it tends to be semi-diurnal. Two samples of recordings from Indonesia at the western end and Indonesia at the eastern end are also given.

articleTitle: Nearshore Circulation Dynamic During Various Monsoon Across Porong River Estuary
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: The estuary of Porong River Sidoarjo receives heavy pressure from a mud volcano eruption that is diverted into the Porong river to prevent wider destruction on the populated area. Due to massive mud discharge, over sedimentation on the estuary of Porong River potentially modifies the pattern of nearshore circulation. This paper investigated the patterns of nearshore circulation within the Porong estuary through observations and numerical models to understand the dynamics of coastal circulation under various seasons. The result showed the influence of astronomic water level variations (range of 2.1 m) and river discharge (average of 33 m/s) to the circulation patterns within the estuary. Further analysis showed the monsoonal variations did not significantly alter the nearshore patterns.

articleTitle: The problem of Microplastic Accumulation in the Arctic Ocean
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Recently, ice in the Northern Arctic Ocean has been rapidly melting. Microplastic debris accumulated in ice has posed a global threat to various marine organisms and ecological processes for many years. In general, microplastics represent marine life, and through them, a person consumes marine products. Microplastics pollute ice, water, water, and fishery organisms that are used for the economy. Microplastic particles (less than 5 mm in size) pose a particular danger to humans due to their high mobility in the marine environment, their ability to be included in the food chain at all levels, the accumulation of various persistent organic pollutants, heavy metals, and other hazardous substances carried by ocean currents over long distances on the surface. Our initial survey shows that microplastics are found in seawater, on the seashore, and the seabed, in ice, and marine life. The research needs to be continued to get a complete picture of microplastic pollution in the Arctic Ocean.

articleTitle: The Hydrodynamics Simulation of Tidal Current in Balikpapan Bay
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Balikpapan is located on the east coast of Kalimantan Island, directly adjacent to the Makassar Straits, and serves as a shipping lane and port city. The hydrodynamic conditions in Balikpapan Bay are essential to know because it dramatically influences the processes that occur. This study will simulate the hydrodynamic pattern of Balikpapan Bay using the Delft3D numerical model by analyzing changes in the depth-averaged velocity and analysis related to the bottom current. The simulation results of the hydrodynamic model for sea-level elevation values are close to the conditions in the field, as indicated by the correlation coefficient 0.98, skill 0.93, and RMSE 0,16 m. The most dominant tidal components are M2 and S2, with a contribution value of 65.3%. In the spring tide conditions, the highest elevation value was 1.55 m, the lowest elevation was -1.42 m, so the tidal range is about 2.99 m. In the neap tide conditions, the highest elevation value was 0.62 m, the lowest elevation was - 0,57 m, so the tidal range was around 1.19 m. The highest current velocity magnitude is at a point B with a value of 0.31 m/s and occurs when flood tide during spring tide. A significant change in the tide when the ebb tide towards high tide at point C, which increases by 680%. Meanwhile, during the neap tide, significant changes occur in ebb tide conditions towards high tide at point B, which increases 689%. Significant changes when spring tide increases by 250% from point C to point D at ebb tide conditions. Meanwhile, significant changes occur from point B to point C at low tide during the neap tide, increasing the magnitude by 338%.

articleTitle: A Rapid Test for Tephra Layer Determination in Marine Core Sediment: Case of SO189/2_04KL in Bengkulu Basin, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Volcanic ash is a high-potential, widespread volcanic product that is commonly used as a marker in geology and archeology. It can be found in marine sediment up to a thousand kilometers from its source (e.g., the Young Tuff Toba). The presence of a volcanic layer in marine sediment is critical for understanding Earth's processes. Here, we test amethod to determine the tephra layer in a marine sediment core. It is SO189/2_04KL from western Sumatra water, specifically in Bengkulu Basin, Indonesia. Using an X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) handheld, chemical composition wasobtained only in the interval 600–800 cm below the seafloor (cmbsf). The visible volcanoclastic unit (VVU) is calculated using three elemental ratios: In (Fe/Ca), In (Mn/Ca), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\text{Fe}+\text{Mn})/(\text{Ca}+\text{Sr})}$</tex>. We also used In (Rb/Sr) and In (Zr/Rb) to differentiate between primary and secondary VVUs. This study found three tephra layers (two VVUp on the intervals of 661- 664 cmbsf and 739–742 cmbsf, and one secondary VVUs layer on the interval of 748–750 cmbsf. We conclude that the elemental ratios In (Fe/Mn), InMn/Ca, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\text{Fe}+\text{Mn})/(\text{Sr}+\text{Ca})}$</tex> could be used to determine the VVU layer, whereas In (Rb/Sr) and In (Zr/Rb) could be used to differentiate primary andsecondary VVU layers.

articleTitle: Buoy Monitoring System in Lombok Strait for The Indonesian Tsunami Coastal Acoustic Tomography (Ina-CAT)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Ina-CAT is an Indonesian Coastal Acoustic Tomography (CAT) system that is applied to the Tsunami Early Warning System (TEWS). Also known as Tsunami Coastal Acoustic Tomography (TCAT), one of these systems was installed in Karangasem-Bali using a buoy platform. TCAT requires power for the electronic system and energy to transmit the acoustic signal through its transducer. The charging system is carried out by installing a solar cell on the surface of the buoy. Thus, a monitoring system is needed to observe the charging process and power consumption. The system also observes the temperature and humidity in the buoy so that the environmental conditions of electronic equipment can be monitored. In addition, the actual position and buoy shift also can be observed. The monitoring system can also serve as early detection of problems when data acquisition does not work properly or the buoy shifts or drifts too far from the initial position. This paper is aimed to discuss the main architecture and sensors utilized in the system. Results indicate that the monitoring system can function properly and be able to monitor power and environmental conditions, yet the charging system needs to be optimized. To improve the accuracy of the monitoring system, sensors that are more precise and calibrated in measurement are required.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Indonesia Cable Based Tsunameter (INA-CBT) Rokatenda Ring Topology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: By this year National Research and Innovation (BRIN) will deploy Indonesia Cable Based Tsunameter (INA-CBT) in Rokatenda, Nusa Tenggara Timur, Indonesia. INA-CBT system has a function to detect tsunami events by installing the submarine cable integrated with the Ocean Bottom Unit (OBU). OBUs are connected to a dedicated specific core for each OBU to the Landing Station (LS). INA- CBT systems were designed by using ring topology and TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) technology. To evaluate the ring topology performance when the failover dan failback event occurs, in this paper we measure the failover time as well as failback time to calculate the duration for each process with different scenarios. Also, we calculate accelerometer data packet loss during the event from each OBUs. We discover that the RK-MANTA ring topology reaches the expected results, where the failover duration average is 262.521 ms and the failback duration average is 107.660ms. Ring topology system design in RK-MANTA shows good performance during failback and failover and complies with the criteria of INA-CBT data transmission requirements

articleTitle: Indonesia's Cable Based Tsunameter (CBT) System as an Earthquake Disaster Mitigation System in East Nusa Tenggara
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Indonesia is located between the Ring of Fire, stretching from Nusa Tenggara, Bali, Java, Sumatra to the Himalayas, Mediterranean, and then culminates in the Atlantic Ocean. Therefore, Indonesia has many active volcanoes that cause earthquakes, such as recently in West Sumatra, Southern Java, and around East Nusa Tenggara (NTT). Disaster mitigation, especially seabed monitoring, is needed as one of the early detection efforts of a seabed earthquake that will potentially become a tsunami disaster. The National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) has developed a marine disaster detection system since 2004 called Indonesia Tsunami Early Warning System (InaTEWS). BRIN has placed several seabed earthquake detectors that spread throughout Indonesian waters from Sumatra to Sorong Papua. The seabed monitoring system described in this paper is the Cable Based Tsunameter (CBT) using a Solar Power Plant developed by BRIN and it will start operating by the end of 2021. The Paper describes the devices used for the CBT system, which will be installed in a location at NTT, and the capacity of the Solar Power Plant is 7kWp to energize the electricity of the CBT system.

articleTitle: Preliminary Research in Tsunami Modelling-Leveraging Artificial Intelligence Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: The advent of modern supercomputers technology, in conjunction with larger, more comprehensive observation datasets, has led to a paradigm shift in early forecasting of Tsunami modeling. Full geological fault parameters of Tsunami wave generation and scenarios, and historical data of earthquakes are routinely employed as tools to estimate propagation properties of the Tsunami wave with high resolution. The Artificial Intelligent (AI) methods fit simulated Tsunami to real-time observed data by iteratively updating estimates of propagation properties. In this paper, we explore approaches to apply AI by preparing a dataset based on a linear tsunami model (TUNAMI) and conducting an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) training constructed based on Random Forest (RF) regression algorithm. AI Performance is assessed through controlled numerical experiments and resulting Tsunami height (SSH) and Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) resulted from both approaches.

articleTitle: Inverse Kinematics Model for a Ship Mounted Two-DoF Manipulator System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: The model of inverse kinematics of a ship-mounted two-DoF manipulator for calculation of the joint angles is substantial due to the randomness of the ocean waves. This paper addresses such a task by investigating the effect of ocean random waves on the inverse kinematics process. Ship motions in terms of a surge, heave, sway, roll, pitch, and yaw motions are produced via Marine Systems Simulator (MSS) toolbox and considered as non-deterministic disturbances at the base of the manipulator. Given the specifications of the ship and manipulator, extensive numerical simulations and their validation are performed. The results reveal that the randomness of ocean waves seems to be appearing on the inverse results due to strong coupling among the ocean waves, manipulator system, and the ship. The latter slows down the iteration process where the computational time follows the increase of sea state code, and the increment has a non-linear trend. The results can be used as a baseline for developing visual servoing based adaptive control for manipulator system stabilization.

articleTitle: Incorporation of Fishing Information into AIS Transmission Messages
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Marine fisheries in developing countries like Indonesia involve many small fishing vessels, which become the backbone of economic activities in fishing villages and the livelihood of small fishermen. We present the development of new methods and algorithms for inserting a new message type into AIS transmission packets to deliver information on potential fish locations to the small fishing ships. The scheme is applied to the AIS class B system by putting the information onto the presently unused, we called Message-33. We have now successfully applied this technology to an AIS class- B system, where messages-33 have been successfully sent and received by the AIS Transceiver device. Data from Message-33 has also been successfully displayed to the monitor device. Thus, if fishermen can receive this message-33 information, then the information can be used by fishermen to guide them to fishing locations. We hope that this fishing information feature on their boats can help fishermen to increase their fishing capacity.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Chaetodontidae Fish Identification Algorithms with Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE Ocean Engineering Technology and Innovation Conference: Ocean Observation, Technology and Innovation in Support of Ocean Decade of Science (OETIC)
abstract: Chaetodontidae fish is one of the indicators of coral reef health, so it is necessary to observe its abundance. Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is expected to be able to identify fish in the waters faster than conventional methods because it can automatically recognize objects that are being recorded by implementing deep learning algorithms in it. This research aims to compare the performance of three algorithms (SSD-MobileNet, Faster-RCNN, and TinyYOLO) and determine the appropriate algorithm to be implemented tothe AUV. Models with the highest to lowest accuracy and precision are Faster-RCNN, SSD-MobileNet, and TinyYOLO. Models with the highest to lowest computing speed are SSD- MobileNet, TinyYOLO, and Faster-RCNN. SSD-MobileNet is stated to have the best performance with a mAP value of about 84.47% and a framerate of about 3.08 fps. The computation speedof SSD-MobileNet, when implemented on the Raspberry Pi, is around 18.02 fps with the addition of the Coral USB Accelerator. This allows the fish identification using the AUV to be accuratein real-time.
